Method

Historical simulation: the last {{SCEN}} overlapping {{H}}-day changes of the ECB rate are applied to today's position. VaR is the loss that is exceeded in only 1% of these scenarios; Expected Shortfall is the average loss in the worst 2.5%.

{{TABLE}}
ApproachEUR% of position

Assumptions and limitations

  • EUR value = USD {{USD}} / rate (rate in USD per 1 EUR). A stronger euro is a loss.
  • The position is held for the full {{H}} trading days; conversion at the ECB reference rate, no bid/ask spread or fees.
  • History is assumed to be representative of the next {{H}} days. Regime changes (e.g. a sudden policy move) are not anticipated.
  • Overlapping {{H}}-day windows share 4 of 5 days, so exceptions cluster and the Kupiec test is too optimistic. A non-overlapping check is shown under the backtest.
  • The Basel traffic light was designed for 1-day VaR; here it is a guide only.
  • VaR says nothing about the size of losses beyond it; ES fills part of that gap.
  • ECB rates are a daily 2:15 pm CET snapshot; intraday moves are not captured.
